Messages.Author: faust
Messages.Body:
I would like to know, which version of Telepathic Counter is right?
The V:TES version says the the bleed is considered blocked.
But the Sabbat version just says reduce bleed and seems to imply that
the bleed was successful.
Which is right? Infact, in case of cards stating different wordings in
different editions, which do I look at? Latest edition? Latest card
errata?

Also, Damage prevention.
When aggrevated damage is done, does cards like "Skin of Rock" block the
damage?
Is it still considered aggrevated and goes thru or is the damage
negated?
example : Vamp A hits Vamp B with 2 points of aggrevated damage.
Vamp B reduces the damage with superior Skin of Rock, thus reducing the
damage to 0.
Does Vamp B still go to torpor because aggrevated damage was done but
loses no blood, lose the blood and goes to torpor(because Skin of Rock
doesn't state stop aggrevated damage) or prevents the 2 point of damage
and goes on fighting?

Messages.Author: Richard D. Zopf
Messages.Body:
faust <fa...@post1.com> wrote:

>I would like to know, which version of Telepathic Counter is right?
>The V:TES version says the the bleed is considered blocked.

It may be only semantics or a typo, but the bleed is not considered
blocked. It is considered unsuccessful if reduced below one.

>But the Sabbat version just says reduce bleed and seems to imply that
>the bleed was successful.
>Which is right? Infact, in case of cards stating different wordings in
>different editions, which do I look at? Latest edition? Latest card
>errata?

Here's what I found:
>>From LSJ's posted clarifications/errata/rulings:

>>Telepathic Counter - reaction (au):
>> Bleeds can be reduced to negative values. A successful negative
>>bleed is treated as a bleed of zero (and is unsuccessful). [TOM 960419]
>> Is played before the bleed is considered successful, so would be played
>>before cards like Spying Mission, which are only played on a
>>successful bleed. [RTR]

Tom Wylie's ruling 960419 states what you need to know. A bleed
reduced to zero or below is considered an unsuccessful action. I
believe this is true of all bleeds and the methodology used to reduce
them (blocking, Archon Investigation, etc.).

>Also, Damage prevention.
>When aggrevated damage is done, does cards like "Skin of Rock" block the
>damage?

Indeed. Cards does ;-)

>Is it still considered aggrevated and goes thru or is the damage
>negated?

Damge is always considered aggravated, but is reduced by one or two
points(depending on inf/sup. fortitude)

>example : Vamp A hits Vamp B with 2 points of aggrevated damage.
>Vamp B reduces the damage with superior Skin of Rock, thus reducing the
>damage to 0.
>Does Vamp B still go to torpor because aggrevated damage was done but
>loses no blood, lose the blood and goes to torpor(because Skin of Rock
>doesn't state stop aggrevated damage) or prevents the 2 point of damage
>and goes on fighting?

Vamp B prevents the two agg.(bless his resilient corpse) and goes on
fighting like a good Methuselah's minion should...

LSJ will likely tell you "damage is damage", meaning a card must
exclude specific damage types (ala Sabbat Resilience), it otherwise
prevents any type. Also, if you're taking 73 normal plus two
aggravated, you can use your Skin of Rock to prevent the two agg., and
go to torpor with no blood (as opposed to being burnt to cinders)
Regards,
R. David Zopf

Messages.Author: LSJ (VtES Rep)
Messages.Body:
faust wrote:
>
> I would like to know, which version of Telepathic Counter is right?
> The V:TES version says the the bleed is considered blocked.

> But the Sabbat version just says reduce bleed and seems to imply that
> the bleed was successful.

The V:tES says nothing about the bleed being blocked.
But it does remind you that bleeds of zero or less are not
considered successful.
The Sabbat version does not have this reminder text, but
it is just reminder text - true wether the card reminds
you or not.

> Which is right? Infact, in case of cards stating different wordings in
> different editions, which do I look at? Latest edition? Latest card
> errata?

Latest card printing with all current errata.

> Also, Damage prevention.
> When aggrevated damage is done, does cards like "Skin of Rock" block the
> damage?

Yes. Damage prevention cards prevent damage.

> Is it still considered aggrevated and goes thru or is the damage
> negated?

The damage is still aggravated, but (if it is all prevented) the
target doesn't go to torpor.

> example : Vamp A hits Vamp B with 2 points of aggrevated damage.
> Vamp B reduces the damage with superior Skin of Rock, thus reducing the
> damage to 0.

He prevents the damage (he doesn't reduce it).
Vamp B keeps all of his blood (needing none to heal, since all of
the damage is prevented) and doesn't go to torpor (since none of
the aggravated damage went unprevented).

> Does Vamp B still go to torpor because aggrevated damage was done but
> loses no blood, lose the blood and goes to torpor(because Skin of Rock
> doesn't state stop aggrevated damage) or prevents the 2 point of damage
> and goes on fighting?

The third.

Hmmmm.... I've never seen that in the rules at all. I know that
aggravated damage is *applied* to a vampire after normal damage is
applied to them so that they are going to torpor when they take the
aggro damage, otherwise they'd take the aggro damage, go to torpor
immediately and then take normal damage which doesn't do anything
really. However, I've *never* seen it that a damage prevention card
prevents normal damage first. the rules on resolving/preventing damage
are....

Damage Prevention
Prevention cards may only be played during strike resolution. [RTR]
Cannot be used to prevent more damage than is dealt. [RTR 961113]

AND

VI. HOW TO RESOLVE DAMAGE (Heal damage/Prevent Destruction).
--------------------------------------------------------
NOTE: Normal damage is resolved before aggravated damage. [RTR]
NOTE: Damage prevention cards can only be played during the strike
resolution
phase of combat (section V.D.2.b). [RTR]
A. Vampires burn one blood to heal each point of normal damage. (8.1)
B. Vampires who cannot heal all of the damage (damage > blood) must
spend all
of their blood and then will be placed in torpor after any
aggravated
damage is applied (see step C).
C. Vampires burn one blood (to prevent destruction) for each point of
aggravated damage. (21)
D. Allies and Retainers burn one life counter for each point of
damage.
E. Check for Vampires going to Torpor or Minions or Retainers burning.
1. If a Vampire cannot pay for all aggravated damage (aggravated
damage
in excess of blood) then it is burned without going to torpor.
(21)
2. Vampires which have taken at least one point of aggravated damage
but
were not burned are placed in Torpor. (21)
3. If a Vampire could not heal all of the damage (damage in excess
of
blood) then it is placed in Torpor with no blood. (21)
4. Allies and Retainers that have zero life counters are burned.
(21)

Nowhere does it say in any of those anything about damage prevention
being done in a specific order. I suppose if you wanted to you could
prevent normal damage first (say, you wanted your vamp to go into torpor
to trigger the Fame on it but not do enough damage to burn it outright
thus not triggering the fame), but there isn't, to my knowledge, an
official ruling on which is prevented first (as far as I'm concerned,
you pick (though I'd normally prevent the agg dam first).

Heh, heh. Well, you asked for it. :>
I think that you have conceptually separated the two lots of damage
too far, so that they must now seem irreconcileable. I completely agree
with your assessment of the example, these are two sources of damage and
can be treated separately. However, your example is quite different to
what a pulled fangs is supposed to represent. The pulled fangs is not a
cigar following a punch. Example to follow.
I play a Torn Signpost with the calm but menacing Helena Casimir. Tusk
is beginning to doubt his controller's wisdom as he pulls out a
disguised bastard sword greeted by a slight eyebrow raise from Helena.
Neither of them maneuver and Helena grabs the slimy Nosfa in an Immortal
Grapple, a hold she learned several centuries ago. Tusk, on the verge of
panic, grunts it up a little with an undead strength, Helena laughs and
shows him how to do it with one of her own. Tusk takes 5 points as the
foaming Ventrue chief whip shows him how to really use potence, and
Helena takes nothing because she has skin of steel! (Clang!)
(- Requirements met, Helena plays a pulled fangs, knocking the poor
Nosfa into torpor with no blood. Assuming he was on full 6 before the
unfortunate encounter)
With a last burst of effort, Helena rams her hand into the sad Nosfa's
mouth reefing out his teeth as the final blow. Helena bends down to
check that he isnt finally dead (they might need him later), delicately
brushes her cloak, and walks off into the night.
The pulled fangs occurs as the result of the last punch, and not as a
seperate incident. Whether the vampire actually pulled out the teeth on
purpose, or if it was the result of massive head trauma isnt clear, and
the card game combat system wisely doesnt go into that detail.
Therefore,
I argue that the pulled fangs is prevented after the punch (or whatever)
because there can be no pulling of fangs if there is no damage. So if
you can prevent the pulled fangs damage, why couldnt you prevent the
damage that caused the pulled fangs? So what im saying (finally) is that
the pulled fangs changes the nature of the hit, rather than hit a second
time. So either you prevent the whole lot, or you take the whole lot.
(phew, that wasnt easy) If Helena hadnt played the pulled fangs Tusk
mightve just gotten squashed with some broken bones or dislocations etc.
something healable at any rate. But the playing of the pulled fangs
results in rewriting the story so that Helena actually rips out his
fangs rather then some other kind of damage. (it might have been better
if I had constructed the story so that I had 2 seperate endings and
could show the difference between them, in terms of story and then game
mechanics, but you can pretend I did)

Im not sure anyone else is reading this thread anymore :>,

James B.

powers severely)
